title: Proteomics Couples Electrical Remodeling to Inflammation in a Murine Model of Heart Failure with Sinus Node Dysfunction
projectDescription: In patients with heart failure, concomitant sinus node dysfunction (SND) is an important predictor of mortality, yet its molecular underpinnings are poorly understood. Here, we acquired deep sinus node proteomes and phosphoproteomes in mice with heart failure and SND and report extensive remodelling. Intersecting the measured (phospho)proteome changes with human genomics and pharmacovigilance data highlighted downregulated proteins involved in electrical activity such as the pacemaker ion channel, Hcn4. We confirmed the importance of ion channel downregulation for sinus node physiology using computer modelling. Guided by the proteomics data, we hypothesized that an inflammatory response may drive the electrophysiological remodeling underlying SND in heart failure. In support of this, experimentally induced inflammation downregulated Hcn4 and slowed pacemaking in the isolated sinus node. From the proteomics data we identified proinflammatory cytokine-like protein galectin-3 as a potential target to mitigate the effect. Indeed, in-vivo suppression of galectin-3 in the animal model of heart failure prevented SND. Collectively, we outline the protein and phosphorylation remodeling of SND in heart failure, we highlight a role for inflammation in electrophysiological remodelling of the sinus node, and we present galectin-3 signalling as a target to ameliorate SND in heart failure.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Tissue homogenization Sinus node (SN) samples were obtained for the heart failure and control group from 15 mice each. Sample preparation was carried out as described earlier (Linscheid et al., 2019). Briefly, tissue samples were homogenized in lysis buffer. Three sinus node samples were pooled into one to obtain five groups each for heart failure and control mice. Protein precipitation was carried out by adding TCA to yield a final of concentration of 4% TCA, incubating for 30 min at 4°C and spinning at 200 x g for 2min. The pellet was resuspended in GdnHCl buffer by intermittent vortexing and heating at 95°C for 5 min. Samples were reduced using 5 mM TCEP and alkylation was carried out using 10 mM CAA and incubating for 15 min in the dark.   Peptide preparation Samples were diluted to yield a final concentration of 2 M GdnHCl using 50 mM Tris pH 8.5 and initial digestion was carried out using Lys-C (Trichem ApS, Denmark; 1:300 enzyme:protein ratio) for 1 h at 37 °C, 750 rpm. Samples were again diluted to yield a final concentration of 0.5 M GdnHCl using 50 mM Tris pH 8.5 and a second digestion was carried out using trypsin (Life technologies, USA, 1:100 enzyme:protein ratio) for 16 h at 37 °C, 750 rpm. The cleared lysates were desalted and concentrated on C18 SepPak columns (Waters, USA). Peptides were eluted twice with 40% acetonitrile (ACN), and organic solvents subsequently evaporated by vacuum centrifugation.   TMT labeling TMT labeling was carried out as described by Zecha et al., 2019. Briefly, 140 µg of each of the ten samples were taken and HEPES pH 8.0 buffer was added to yield a final concentration of 50 mM. NaOH was added in case the pH was not reached. 200 µg of TMT10-plex reagents (Thermo Fisher) was added from stocks dissolved in 100 % anhydrous ACN such that the final mix had 4 µg/µl peptide, 20% ACN, 50 mM HEPES pH 8.0, vortexed immediately and incubated at room temperature for 1 h at 1000 rpm. The reaction was quenched by adding hydroxylamine to yield a final concentration of 1% hydroxylamine and incubated at room temperature for 15 min at 1000 rpm. All the ten labelled samples were pooled, and 300 µg of pooled peptide sample was acidified using TFA to yield a final concentration of 2% TFA, the organic content evaporated using vacuum centrifugation and finally desalted on C18 SepPak columns (Waters, USA). The SepPaks columns were stored at 4 °C until elution and subsequent fractionation. The rest of the pooled peptides (~1 mg) were further processed for phosphopeptide enrichment.   Off-line peptide fractionation Fractionation was carried out by micro-flow reverse-phase ultra-high-pressure liquid chromatography (UPLC) on a Dionex UltiMate 3000 UPLC system (Thermo Scientific, USA) equipped with an Dionex Ultimate 3000 using a Thermo Acclaim PA2 column (3 µm, 300 µm x 150 mm) using a flow rate of 15 µl/min. TMT labeled samples were fractionated (into 78 fractions) using a 87 min linear gradient as described by Bekker-Jensen et al., 2017. The first five fractions were combined into one, and after that every two fractions were combined to eventually obtain a total of 38 fractions. Phosphopeptide samples were fractionated into 12 fractions whereby the outflow from 4–60 min was collected at 1 min intervals into 12 concatenated fractions in the autosampler. ~200-300 ng of peptides were injected for the TMT labeled samples. For the phosphopeptide samples, the whole sample was injected.  Mass spectrometry measurements  The samples were analyzed by online reversed-phase liquid chromatography coupled to a Q-Exactive HF-X quadrupole Orbitrap tandem mass spectrometer (LC-MS/MS, Thermo Electron, Bremen, Germany). Approximately 200-300 ng of each fraction was autosampled into a nanoflow Easy-nLC system (Proxeon Biosystems, Odense, Denmark) and separated on in-house pulled and packed 15 cm fused-silica emitter columns with reversed-phase ReproSil-Pur C18-AQ 1.9 μm resin (Dr. Maisch GmbH, Ammerbuch-Entringen, Germany) in a 30 min multi-step linear gradient (Buffer A, 0.1% formic acid; Buffer B, 0.1% formic acid, 80% ACN; 10-30% Buffer B in 25 min, 30-45% Buffer B in 5 min, 45-80% Buffer B in 30 s). Column effluent was directly ionized in a nano-electrospray ionization source operated in positive ionization mode and electrosprayed into the mass spectrometer. Full-MS spectra (375-1400 m/z) were acquired upon accumulation of 3e6 ions in the Orbitrap (maximum fill time of 50 ms) at a resolution of 120,000. A data-dependent Top10 method then sequentially isolated the most intense precursor ions for higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) in an octopole collision cell. MS/MS spectra of fragment ions were subsequently recorded at 60,000 resolution after accumulation of 1e5 ions in the Orbitrap (maximum fill time of 100 ms) with normalized collision energy set to 32.
dataProcessingProtocol: Proteome raw data processing MS raw data was processed using MaxQuant v1.6.10.43 (Max-Planck Institute of Biochemistry, Department of Proteomics and Signal Transduction, Munich) by searching MS/MS spectra against the UniProtKB Swiss-Prot Mus musculus database including isoforms (February 2020 release) and including common contaminants. In silico digestion mode was set to Specific, Enzyme to Trypsin/P and up to 2 missed cleavages were allowed. Carbamidomethyl (C) was selected as fixed modification as well as oxidation (M) and Acetyl (protein N-term) as variable modifications. A maximum of five modifications per peptide were allowed, match between runs was enabled and at least one unique peptide was required per protein group to be reported as identified. The results were FDR controlled on PSM level (0.01) and protein level (0.01). Quantification was performed on MS2 level based on TMT Reporter ions applying the appropriate correction factors. Modified peptides, with exception of carbamidomethylated peptides, and MS/MS spectra with a precursor intensity fraction (PIF) below 0.75 were disregarded for quantification. Default setting were used for the remaining parameters.  Phosphoproteome raw data processing MS raw data were processed using MaxQuant v1.6.10.43 (Max-Planck Institute of Biochemistry, Department of Proteomics and Signal Transduction, Munich) by searching MS/MS spectra against the UniProtKB Swiss-Prot Mus musculus database without isoforms (February 2020 release) and including common contaminants. In silico digestion mode was set to Specific, Enzyme to Trypsin/P and up to 2 missed cleavages were allowed. Carbamidomethyl (C) was selected as fixed modification as well as phosphorylation (STY), oxidation (M) and Acetyl (protein N-term) as variable modifications. A maximum of five modifications per peptide were allowed, match between runs was enabled and at least one unique peptide was required per protein group to be reported as identified. The results were FDR controlled on PSM level (0.01) and protein level (0.01). Quantification was performed on MS2 level based on TMT Reporter ions applying the appropriate correction factors. Modified peptides, with exception of carbamidomethylated peptides, and MS/MS spectra with a precursor intensity fraction (PIF) below 0.75 were disregarded for quantification. Default settings were used for the remaining parameters.
